title: Closed horizontal support under a universally submersive map still covers the base
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] and Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Assume $f$ is universally submersive: for every scheme morphism $T\to Y$, the map of underlying spaces $|X\times_Y T|\to |T|$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is surjective and a subset of $|T|$ is open if and only if its inverse image is open. Let $U\subseteq Y$ be a dense open subscheme, where dense means that its topological closure is all of $|Y|$. For every closed subset $Z\subseteq |X|$ containing $f^{-1}(|U|)$, one has $f(Z)=|Y|$.

source.place: Tag 0ETT, lemma-Noetherian-h-covering, proof, last paragraph: the DVR specialization argument after flattening; apply the same argument to a closed subset containing the inverse image of a dense open. The trait through a specified point is supplied there by limits.tex Tag 0CM2, lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian.

proof.text: Write $j:U\hookrightarrow Y$ for the given open inclusion. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-open-closed-finite-presentation] with $S=Y$, $W=U$ and $i=\mathrm{id}_U$ (the closed immersion defined by the zero ideal). Its Noetherian hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis on $Y$, and its conclusion makes $j$ quasi-compact. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] makes $j$ of finite type. Since $U$ is dense, $\overline{j(|U|)}=|Y|$.

source.place: Tag 0ETT, flat-lemma-Noetherian-h-covering, proof, last paragraph: trait through a point and universal-submersivity contradiction; using limits.tex Tag 0CM2 only at a point outside the dense open.

proof.text: Fix $y\in|Y|$. If $y\in U$, surjectivity of $f$ (the identity-base-change case of universal submersivity) gives $x\in X$ over $y$, and then $x\in f^{-1}(U)\subseteq Z$. Otherwise $y\in\overline{j(|U|)}\setminus j(|U|)$. Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-image-boundary-dvr] to the finite-type map $j:U\to Y$, with the locally Noetherian target $Y$. It supplies a DVR $A$, its fraction field $K$, and $g:T=\operatorname{Spec}A\to Y$ whose closed point $s$ maps to $y$ and whose restriction along $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ factors through $U$.

source.place: Tag 0CM2, limits-lemma-reach-point-closure-Noetherian, applied to the open inclusion at a point outside its image; this avoids the trivial-specialization issue in the unrestricted printed statement.

proof.text: Form $W=X\times_Y T$ with projections $p:W\to X$ and $q:W\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $f\circ p=g\circ q$. Universal submersivity, applied to $g$, says that $q$ is surjective and that a subset of $T$ is open exactly when its inverse image under $q$ is open. Put $C=p^{-1}(Z)$. This is closed, since morphisms of schemes are continuous [def-pc-scheme]. If $\eta$ denotes the zero prime of $A$, the map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to T$ has image $\eta$: contraction of the zero prime under $A\hookrightarrow K$ is zero [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Therefore $g(\eta)\in U$, and the commuting square gives $q^{-1}(\{\eta\})\subseteq C$.

source.place: Tag 0ETT, flat-lemma-Noetherian-h-covering, proof, last paragraph: trait through a point and universal-submersivity contradiction; using limits.tex Tag 0CM2 only at a point outside the dense open.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one] and the prime-chain definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $T$ has just the points $\eta=(0)$ and $s=\mathfrak m_A$. Indeed $A$ is a local domain with $\mathfrak m_A\ne0$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]; any third prime would give the length-two strict chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak m_A$, contradicting $\dim A=1$. The singleton $\{\eta\}$ is not closed: in the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a closed set $V(I)$ containing $(0)$ has $I\subseteq(0)$, hence $I=(0)$ and $V(I)=T$, which also contains the distinct point $s$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, algebra-lemma-characterize-dvr, (1) implies (3), followed by the definitions of Krull dimension and the Zariski topology.

proof.text: If $C$ had no point over $s$, the two-point description and $q^{-1}(\{\eta\})\subseteq C$ would give $C=q^{-1}(\{\eta\})$. Since $C$ is closed, $q^{-1}(\{s\})=W\setminus C$ would be open. The open-set criterion for $q$ would make $\{s\}$ open in $T$, so $\{\eta\}$ would be closed, contradicting step 4. Hence there is $w\in C$ with $q(w)=s$. Then $p(w)\in Z$ and $f(p(w))=g(q(w))=g(s)=y$. The two cases cover every $y\in|Y|$, proving $f(Z)=|Y|$.
